questions.text: Why summarize MFCC frames using per-coefficient means and variances before k-NN classification?

options.A: To retain the exact temporal order of every phoneme.
options.B: To obtain a fixed-size vector from clips with different frame counts.
options.C: To turn each clip into a manually aligned text transcript.
options.D: To guarantee perfect classification without labeled examples.

questions.explanation: Pooling across time yields a fixed-size embedding (twice the coefficient count), regardless of the number of frames, while discarding temporal order.

questions.text: A sound clip may contain both a siren and barking. Which output-and-loss pairing supports these simultaneous labels?

options.A: One softmax output with exactly one class selected.
options.B: A scalar regression output trained on the alphabetic class index.
options.C: Independent sigmoid outputs with binary cross-entropy.
options.D: A forced blank label whenever two events overlap.

questions.explanation: Multi-label classification needs independent per-class probabilities; binary cross-entropy supports more than one positive label per clip.

questions.text: summarize returns per-coefficient means followed by population variances, dividing squared deviations by the number of frames. For frames [[2], [6]], what does it return?
questions.explanation: The mean is4. Squared deviations are4 and4, and their population average is4, so the result is[4,4].
